servos.name: SG90 9 g micro servo (plastic gears)
servos.source: Typical TowerPro SG90 datasheet figures (4.8 V: 1.8 kg·cm, 0.12 s/60°; ~650–750 mA stall measured across hobby sources). Verify with the units you buy.

servos.name: MG90S 13 g micro servo (metal gears)
servos.source: Typical TowerPro MG90S datasheet figures (4.8 V: 1.8 kg·cm / 0.10 s; 6 V: 2.2 kg·cm). Stall current is not on the datasheet; 700–800 mA is the commonly measured range.

servos.name: MG996R 55 g standard servo (metal gears)
servos.source: Typical TowerPro MG996R figures (6 V: 11 kg·cm, 0.17 s/60°; stall ~2.5 A). Neck and jaw class.

servos.name: DS3218 20 kg·cm digital servo (waterproof)
servos.source: Typical DS3218 listing figures (6.8 V: 20–21 kg·cm, 0.16 s/60°, 270° variant). Stall current is a commonly quoted ~3 A; verify.

servos.name: Feetech STS3215 serial bus servo (7.4 V)
servos.source: Feetech STS3215 product figures (7.4 V: 19.5 kg·cm, 0.222 s/60°, 360° position mode, 12-bit encoder, position/load/temperature readback). The pulse range here is a pulse-equivalent for this contract: a bus servo takes a position word, which the serial-bus controller derives from the same angle. The AM-ARM family uses this class.

controllers.name: PCA9685 16-channel 12-bit PWM driver
controllers.notes: I²C at 0x40 (62 addresses chainable); V+ servo rail is a SEPARATE terminal from VCC logic — feed it 5–6 V at the servos' summed current and share only ground with the microcontroller. Set the PWM frequency to 50 Hz.
controllers.source: NXP PCA9685 datasheet; Adafruit 16-channel servo driver guide.

controllers.name: ESP32 DevKit (USB CDC, Wi-Fi)
controllers.notes: 3.3 V logic drives a PCA9685 and most 5 V hobby servos' signal pins directly. Never power servos from the module's 5 V pin.

controllers.name: Arduino Nano / Uno (ATmega328P)
controllers.notes: 5 V logic. The Servo library drives up to 12 outputs directly; a PCA9685 over I²C is the usual path past two or three servos. Never power servos from the USB 5 V.
